finding: price_for executes pricing.py out of the checkout's .claude/adapters whenever LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON is unset (the production default; every test sets it).

finding: jq programs bind and read $label (pipeline-run.sh:702/708, 816/826, 881/882) and use the {name, label, ...} shorthand (ablation-row.sh:285); jq 1.6 treats label as a keyword and refuses both, so every run dies infrastructure_error at its first run_phase and no row can be built. The tool check at :167 verifies presence only.
reasoning_trace: Reproduced on this host (jq-1.6): `jq -n --arg label x '$label'` -> syntax error, unexpected label; `{label}` -> syntax error; `{label: 1}` is accepted so plan_phases (:224-225) is unaffected.
critique: Undeclared jq >= 1.7 dependency; Debian bookworm (the image base, Dockerfile.ablation:22) ships 1.6.
remediation: Rename the binding (--arg lbl) and write label: .label / "label":; add a jq feature probe beside the tool check or declare the minimum version.

finding: On jq 1.6 raw-slurp drops the trailing NUL, so .[:-1] discards the last real element of argv, env and launcher captures: the value after --effort, the id after --resume, the last env entry (LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false for A4). took-effect rules effort_flag_medium, enforce_env_false and implementer_single_session then report false misses, which DEC-0418 treats as infrastructure_error and pauses the arm.
reasoning_trace: Reproduced: printf 'a\0b\0' | jq -Rsc 'split("\u0000") | .[:-1]' -> ["a"] on jq-1.6. The review reproduced 10 bats failures after fixing CQ-003 alone.
critique: Silent evidence corruption; the phase itself runs with the right argv.
remediation: Build arrays with jq -n '$ARGS.positional' --args "${cargv[@]}" (works on 1.6 and 1.7); add a bats case asserting the last argv element and last env key.

finding: The System Zone count now reads index entries, so a tracked file deleted from the working tree no longer changes the count (previous find did), and an untracked file planted under .claude/ no longer changes it either (DISS-C-002 of the audit dissent). The count check can no longer see either direction of drift.
reasoning_trace: Reproduced: repo with 2 tracked files, one deleted -> ls-files 2, find 1. Review dissent DISS-001 (BLOCKING) raised the deletion case; audit dissent DISS-C-002 raised the addition case.
critique: The fast integrity gate that runs before check-loa.sh now only restates the manifest length.
remediation: Count tracked paths that exist (filter ls-files through [[ -f ]], as gen-checksums.sh:96-100 does) and keep a find-based count for untracked additions, or drop the count check in favour of check-manifest-paths.sh semantics.

finding: make_home copies the operator's codex auth.json under <run>/meta/home; finish/on_exit remove it, but the header (:104-106) documents that a SIGKILLed driver leaves the run directory behind, so the credential copy survives in an archived run tree.

finding: The evaluated agent (bypassPermissions, Bash tool, --network bridge) can read the operator's codex OAuth credential at /home/evaluser/.codex/auth.json and AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK from its environment. Both are needed for the sandbox gates to dispatch, so this is a design acceptance, but a prompt-injected agent working over untrusted fixture content can exfiltrate long-lived operator credentials.
reasoning_trace: Source S8 to sinks K6/K7; the token is kept out of argv and captures (recorded <set>), which is correct, but it is necessarily present in the container environment.
remediation: Use short-lived, scoped credentials for ablation batches (a dedicated codex account, a Bedrock token minted per batch with a TTL) and document the exposure in the Dockerfile header; consider an egress allowlist for the bridge network.

finding: In a submodule mount every manifest path absent locally but present under .loa/<path> is informational; the check has no record of which paths the mount linked, so a deliberately deleted hook or gate script symlink is indistinguishable from a path the mount never links. Confirmed by the audit dissent (DISS-C-001).
reasoning_trace: Read check_integrity in full; mount-submodule.sh prints Linked lines (fresh-mount-proof.sh:157 counts them) but nothing persists the set.
remediation: Record the linked set at mount time and treat an absent path in that set as Missing.
